transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you could make it in today. What brings you in to see me?

Well, hello. Thank you for seeing me. I suppose I'm here because my daughter suggested it. She says I'm just... well, she says I'm always up and moving. And I suppose she's right. Even on a quiet day, I'm bouncing from the garden club list to my knitting bag to travel papers before I've really finished any one thing. Oh, speaking of travel papers, my husband and I went to Florida last winter, and you wouldn't believe the humidity! My hair was just an absolute disaster the entire time. We stayed at this lovely little place right on the beach, though. They had these wonderful little complimentary soaps in the bathroom, shaped like seashells. I brought a whole bag of them home for the guest bath. Anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, my daughter thinks I just can't seem to sit still and finish a project.
Have you been this way for as long as you can remember since childhood, or is this something that started more recently?

Oh my, no, this isn't a new thing at all. It's been my whole life, really. Even back in grade school, my teachers used to tell my mother that I was a bright girl, but just terribly scattered. I was always losing my papers. 

Which reminds me, I just lost my favorite recipe card for peach cobbler the other day! I was going to make it for the church bake sale. We have a bake sale every spring to raise money for the choir robes, and let me tell you, those robes are getting so worn out. The hems on the tenor section are just fraying to bits, and I told Pastor Dave we really need to look into a different dry cleaner because the chemicals they use are just too harsh on the fabric. 

But oh, where was I? Right, grade school. Yes, my teachers said I was always talking out of turn, just chatting away, and wiggling around in my seat before I ever finished my work. I just couldn't seem to sit still even back then.
Do you ever have times where you can get by on very little sleep, like just a few hours, and still feel completely energized?

Oh, goodness, no. If I only get a few hours of sleep, I am just dragging the next day. I really need my solid seven or eight hours. 

We actually just bought a new mattress last year because my back was starting to bother me on the old one. We went down to that big furniture place on Route 4... oh, what's it called? Mattress King? Something like that. Anyway, the salesman there was wearing the loudest plaid suit I have ever seen in my life. It was bright yellow and green! I whispered to my husband, "He looks like a walking lemon-lime soda." My husband just shushed me—he hates when I make comments like that in public—but I couldn't help it! 

We ended up buying a memory foam one, which is lovely, but it is just so heavy to lift when you're putting the fitted sheet on. I always have to buy the deep-pocket sheets now because the regular ones just pop right off the corners in the middle of the night, and there is nothing worse than waking up sleeping on a bare mattress pad. I found a lovely set on sale at the department store, a very soft lavender color... 

But... oh, wait, what were you asking me? About sleep? Right, yes, I definitely need my sleep. I've never been one of those people who can just run on fumes and feel energized, that's for sure.

Well, I suppose they do cause some problems, yes. It's really started causing a strain at home, and over at the community center, too. My husband gets so frustrated because he says he can't count on me to keep our plans straight. And the other volunteers at the center are starting to feel the same way. They feel like someone always has to check behind me to make sure I've actually done what I said I'd do. 

Like last week, I was supposed to organize the canned goods for the food drive. We do a big food drive every Thanksgiving, and people are so generous, they really are. But you wouldn't believe how many people donate expired cans! I found a can of cranberry sauce from 2018! Who keeps cranberry sauce for five years? And it was the jellied kind, too. I always prefer the whole berry kind myself, it just tastes more authentic, don't you think? My mother used to make it from scratch, boiling the berries on the stove until they popped. The whole house would smell so wonderful and tart. 

Anyway, I was supposed to be sorting the cans by expiration date, but I got to chatting with Mrs. Higgins—she just had her hip replaced, you know, and she was telling me all about the physical therapy, which sounds just dreadful—and I ended up putting the vegetables with the soups, and I completely forgot to check the dates on half the boxes. The center director had to come in and redo the whole thing. So... yes, I guess you could say my scattering about does interfere with things quite a bit.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient demonstrates persistent, pervasive symptoms of both inattention (frequently jumping between unfinished tasks, losing items, disorganization, high distractibility) and hyperactivity-impulsivity (constant motor restlessness, excessive talking, difficulty remaining seated). These symptoms have been present since childhood (elementary school) across multiple settings and cause clear functional impairment in domestic life and volunteer work, fulfilling criteria for F90.0. A manic/hypomanic episode is ruled out by normal sleep requirements and absence of decreased need for sleep.
